subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Flow Measurement: How Much Is Moving?
description: A quick, practical guide to Flow Measurement: How Much Is Moving?.

hook.text: You can't manage what you can't measure. Flow meters make flow visible.

buildup.text: Orifice plates restrict flow and create a pressure drop proportional to speed.

discovery.text: Ultrasonic meters bounce sound through the fluid to measure velocity.

twist.text: Magnetic flow meters work only on conductive fluids. Water yes, oil no.

climax.text: Water utilities, oil refineries, and breweries all rely on flow metering.

punchline.text: Measure the flow and you control the process.

quiz.question: Why can't magnetic flow meters measure oil flow?
options: Oil is too viscous for the meter to detect
Magnetic meters need a conductive fluid, and oil doesn't conduct electricity
Oil damages the meter's magnetic sensors
